title: Exercise (A1)
content: Define what it means for \(T \in \cL(V, W)\) to be an isomorphism, and what \(V \cong W\) means. True or false: \(\nR[x]_{\le 3} \cong M_2(\nR)\) . Justify your answer. title: Exercise (B1: An explicit isomorphism)

title: Exercise (C1: Invertible products)
content: Let \(V\) be finite-dimensional and \(S, T \in \cL(V)\) . Prove that if \(ST\) is invertible, then \(S\) and \(T\) are both invertible. Deduce that \(TS\) is then invertible too. title: Theorem 3.5.1 (The Inverse of a Linear Bijection Is Linear)
content: Let \(T \in \cL(V, W)\) be bijective. Then its inverse function \(T^{-1} \colon W \to V\) is linear. Consequently, a linear map \(T\) is invertible if and only if it is bijective.

title: Theorem 3.5.7 (Invertible Operator Theorem)
content: Let \(V\) be a finite-dimensional vector space over \(F\) , and let \(T \in \cL(V)\) . The following are equivalent. \(T\) is invertible. \(T\) is injective. \(\ker T = \{\0\}\) , that is, \(\nullity T = 0\) . \(T\) is surjective. \(\rank T = \dim V\) . There is \(S \in \cL(V)\) with \(ST = \id_V\) . There is \(S \in \cL(V)\) with \(TS = \id_V\) . \(T\) maps some basis of \(V\) to a basis of \(V\) . \(T\) maps every basis of \(V\) to a basis of \(V\) .

title: Theorem 3.5.3 (Isomorphism Is an Equivalence Relation)
content: For vector spaces over \(F\) : \(V \cong V\) ; if \(V \cong W\) then \(W \cong V\) ; and if \(U \cong V\) and \(V \cong W\) then \(U \cong W\) .

title: Theorem 3.5.4 (Classification of Finite-Dimensional Spaces)
content: Let \(V\) and \(W\) be finite-dimensional vector spaces over the same field \(F\) . Then \[ V \cong W \quad \iff \quad \dim V = \dim W . \]

title: Theorem 3.5.2 (Isomorphisms Carry Bases to Bases)
content: Let \(T \colon V \to W\) be an isomorphism, and let \((\v_1, \dots, \v_n)\) be a basis of \(V\) . Then \((T\v_1, \dots, T\v_n)\) is a basis of \(W\) .

title: Theorem 3.5.6 (One-Sided Inverses of Linear Maps)
content: Let \(V\) and \(W\) be finite-dimensional vector spaces over \(F\) with \(\dim V = \dim W\) . Let \(T \in \cL(V, W)\) and \(S \in \cL(W, V)\) . If \(ST = \id_V\) , then \(TS = \id_W\) . In that case \(T\) and \(S\) are both isomorphisms, \(S = T^{-1}\) and \(T = S^{-1}\) .

title: Corollary 3.6.3 (Matrices of Powers and Polynomials)
page: 3.6 The Matrix of a Linear Map
content: Let \(\sB = (\v_1, \dots, \v_n)\) be a basis of a finite-dimensional space \(V\) , let \(T, S \in \cL(V)\) , \(c \in F\) and \(p \in F[x]\) . Then \([ST]_{\sB} = [S]_{\sB}[T]_{\sB}\) , \([S + T]_{\sB} = [S]_{\sB} + [T]_{\sB}\) , \([cT]_{\sB} = c[T]_{\sB}\) , \([T^k]_{\sB} = ([T]_{\sB})^k\) for \(k \in \nN\) , and \[ [p(T)]_{\sB} = p\bigl([T]_{\sB}\bigr). \]

title: Definition 3.6.1 (Matrix of a Linear Map)
page: 3.6 The Matrix of a Linear Map
content: Let \(V\) and \(W\) be finite-dimensional vector spaces over \(F\) , with ordered bases \(\sB = (\v_1, \dots, \v_n)\) of \(V\) and \(\sC = (\w_1, \dots, \w_m)\) of \(W\) , and let \(T \in \cL(V, W)\) . The matrix of \(T\) with respect to \(\sB\) and \(\sC\) is the \(m \times n\) matrix \[ \mtx{T}{\sB}{\sC} \coloneqq \begin{pmatrix} \coord{T\v_1}{\sC} & \coord{T\v_2}{\sC} & \cdots & \coord{T\v_n}{\sC} \end{pmatrix} \in M_{m \times n}(F), \] whose \(j\) -th column is the coordinate vector of \(T\v_j\) with respect to \(\sC\) . Equivalently, its entries \(a_{ij}\) are the unique scalars with \[ T\v_j = a_{1j}\w_1 + a_{2j}\w_2 + \dots + a_{mj}\w_m \qquad (j = 1, \dots, n). \] When \(V = W\) and \(\sB = \sC\) , we write \([T]_{\sB} \coloneqq \mtx{T}{\sB}{\sB}\) and call it the matrix of the operator \(T\) with respect to \(\sB\) .

title: Theorem 3.6.4 (\cL(V, W) \cong M_{m \times n}(F))
page: 3.6 The Matrix of a Linear Map
content: Let \(V\) and \(W\) be finite-dimensional vector spaces over \(F\) with ordered bases \(\sB = (\v_1, \dots, \v_n)\) and \(\sC = (\w_1, \dots, \w_m)\) . Then the map \[ \Phi \colon \cL(V, W) \to M_{m \times n}(F), \qquad T \mapsto \mtx{T}{\sB}{\sC}, \] is an isomorphism. In particular, \(\dim \cL(V, W) = mn = (\dim V)(\dim W)\) .

title: Theorem 3.6.2 (Matrix of a Composition)
page: 3.6 The Matrix of a Linear Map
content: Let \(U, V, W\) be finite-dimensional vector spaces over \(F\) with ordered bases \(\sB\) , \(\sC\) , \(\sD\) respectively. Let \(T \in \cL(U, V)\) and \(S \in \cL(V, W)\) . Then \[ \mtx{ST}{\sB}{\sD} = \mtx{S}{\sC}{\sD}\,\mtx{T}{\sB}{\sC} . \]

title: Theorem 3.6.1 (Coordinates of an Image)
page: 3.6 The Matrix of a Linear Map
content: Let \(V\) and \(W\) be finite-dimensional vector spaces over \(F\) with ordered bases \(\sB = (\v_1, \dots, \v_n)\) and \(\sC = (\w_1, \dots, \w_m)\) , and let \(T \in \cL(V, W)\) . Then for every \(\v \in V\) , \[ \coord{T\v}{\sC} = \mtx{T}{\sB}{\sC}\,\coord{\v}{\sB} . \] Moreover, \(\mtx{T}{\sB}{\sC}\) is the only matrix \(A \in M_{m \times n}(F)\) with \(\coord{T\v}{\sC} = A\coord{\v}{\sB}\) for all \(\v \in V\) .

title: Theorem 3.6.5 (Rank and Invertibility from the Matrix)
page: 3.6 The Matrix of a Linear Map
content:
Let \(V\) and \(W\) be finite-dimensional vector spaces over \(F\) with ordered bases \(\sB\) and \(\sC\) , let \(T \in \cL(V, W)\) , and let \(A = \mtx{T}{\sB}{\sC}\) . The coordinate map \(\v \mapsto \coord{\v}{\sB}\) restricts to an isomorphism \(\ker T 	o 
ul(A)\) , and the coordinate map \(\w \mapsto \coord{\w}{\sC}\) restricts to an isomorphism \(\im T 	o \col(A)\) . Hence \[ ank T = ank A \qquad 	ext{and} \qquad 
ullity T = 
ullity A . \] Suppose \(\dim V = \dim W\) . Then \(T\) is invertible if and only if \(A\) is invertible, and in that case \(\mtx{T^{-1}}{\sC}{\sB} = A^{-1}\) .

title: Definition 3.7.1 (Change-of-coordinates matrix)
content: Let \(V\) be a finite-dimensional vector space over \(F\) , and let \(\sB = (\v_1, \dots, \v_n)\) and \(\sC\) be ordered bases of \(V\) . The change-of-coordinates matrix from \(\sB\) to \(\sC\) is the \(n \times n\) matrix \[ \mtx{\id}{\sB}{\sC} \coloneqq \mtx{\id_V}{\sB}{\sC}, \] the matrix of the identity map \(\id_V \colon V \to V\) with respect to the input basis \(\sB\) and the output basis \(\sC\) . Its \(j\) -th column is \(\coord{\v_j}{\sC}\) .

title: Definition 3.7.2 (Similar matrices)
content: Let \(A, B \in M_n(F)\) . We say \(A\) is similar to \(B\) , written \(A \sim B\) , if there exists an invertible matrix \(P \in M_n(F)\) such that \[ B = P^{-1}AP . \]

title: Proposition 3.7.2 (Invertible matrices are changes of basis)
content: Let \(\sB = (\v_1, \dots, \v_n)\) be a basis of \(V\) , and let \(P = (p_{ij}) \in M_n(F)\) be invertible. Put \[ \v_j' \coloneqq p_{1j}\v_1 + p_{2j}\v_2 + \dots + p_{nj}\v_n \qquad (j = 1, \dots, n). \] Then \(\sB' = (\v_1', \dots, \v_n')\) is a basis of \(V\) , and \(\mtx{\id}{\sB'}{\sB} = P\) .

title: Proposition 3.7.6 (More similarity invariants)
content: Let \(A, B \in M_n(F)\) with \(B = P^{-1}AP\) for an invertible \(P\) . \(\rank A = \rank B\) . \(A\) is invertible if and only if \(B\) is invertible. For every polynomial \(p \in F[x]\) , \(p(B) = P^{-1}p(A)P\) . In particular, \(p(A) = 0\) if and only if \(p(B) = 0\) ; for example, \(A^2 = 0\) if and only if \(B^2 = 0\) .

title: Theorem 3.7.3 (Change of Basis for Linear Maps)
content: Let \(V\) and \(W\) be finite-dimensional vector spaces over \(F\) , let \(\sB, \sB'\) be bases of \(V\) and \(\sC, \sC'\) bases of \(W\) , and let \(T \colon V \to W\) be linear. Then \[ \mtx{T}{\sB'}{\sC'} = \mtx{\id}{\sC}{\sC'}\,\mtx{T}{\sB}{\sC}\,\mtx{\id}{\sB'}{\sB}. \] In particular, for an operator \(T \in \cL(V)\) and bases \(\sB, \sB'\) of \(V\) , with \(P = \mtx{\id}{\sB'}{\sB}\) , \[ [T]_{\sB'} = P^{-1}\,[T]_{\sB}\,P . \]

title: Theorem 3.7.1 (Change of Coordinates)
content: Let \(V\) be a vector space of dimension \(n\) , and let \(\sB\) , \(\sC\) , \(\sD\) be bases of \(V\) . For every \(\v \in V\) , \(\coord{\v}{\sC} = \mtx{\id}{\sB}{\sC}\coord{\v}{\sB}\) . Moreover, \(\mtx{\id}{\sB}{\sC}\) is the only matrix \(M \in M_n(F)\) with \(\coord{\v}{\sC} = M\coord{\v}{\sB}\) for every \(\v \in V\) . \(\mtx{\id}{\sB}{\sD} = \mtx{\id}{\sC}{\sD}\mtx{\id}{\sB}{\sC}\) . \(\mtx{\id}{\sB}{\sC}\) is invertible, and \(\big(\mtx{\id}{\sB}{\sC}\big)^{-1} = \mtx{\id}{\sC}{\sB}\) .

title: Theorem 3.7.4 (Similar Matrices Represent the Same Operator)
content: Let \(A, B \in M_n(F)\) . If \(V\) is a vector space of dimension \(n\) , \(T \in \cL(V)\) , and \(\sB, \sC\) are bases of \(V\) , then \([T]_{\sB} \sim [T]_{\sC}\) . Conversely, suppose \(A \sim B\) . Let \(V\) be any vector space of dimension \(n\) with a basis \(\sB\) , and let \(T \in \cL(V)\) be an operator with \([T]_{\sB} = A\) . Then there is a basis \(\sC\) of \(V\) with \([T]_{\sC} = B\) . Such an operator \(T\) in (b) always exists. In particular, \(A \sim B\) if and only if \(A\) and \(B\) are the matrices of the operator \(\x \mapsto A\x\) on \(F^n\) in the standard basis and in some basis of \(F^n\) , respectively.

title: Theorem 3.7.5 (Trace Is a Similarity Invariant)
content: If \(A, B \in M_n(F)\) are similar, then \(\tr A = \tr B\) .

title: Definition 3.8.1 (Equivalent matrices)
content: Let \(A, B \in M_{m \times n}(F)\) . We say \(A\) is equivalent to \(B\) if there exist invertible matrices \(Q \in M_m(F)\) and \(P \in M_n(F)\) such that \[ B = QAP . \]

title: Example (A column–row factorization)
content: Find the column–row factorization of \(A = \begin{pmatrix} 1 & 2 & 0 & 3 \\ 2 & 4 & 1 & 4 \\ 3 & 6 & 1 & 7 \end{pmatrix} \in M_{3 \times 4}(\nR)\) .

title: Example (Bringing a 2 \times 3 matrix to normal form)
content:
Let \(A =  egin{pmatrix} 1 & 2 & 1 \ 2 & 4 & 3 \end{pmatrix} \in M_{2 	imes 3}(
R)\) . Find invertible \(Q \in M_2(
R)\) and \(P \in M_3(
R)\) with \(QAP = N_r\) .

title: Exercise (A1)
content: Define what it means for \(A, B \in M_{m \times n}(F)\) to be equivalent. State the Rank Normal Form theorem for a matrix \(A \in M_{m \times n}(F)\) . True or false: equivalent square matrices are similar. Justify your answer. True or false: \(\rank(AB) = \rank(BA)\) for all \(A, B \in M_n(F)\) . Justify your answer. How many equivalence classes does \(M_{2 \times 5}(\nF_7)\) have? In the proof of the normal form for \(T \colon V \to W\) , which vectors form the end of the basis of \(V\) , and which vectors form the start of the basis of \(W\) ?

title: Exercise (B1: A column–row factorization)
content: Find the column–row factorization of \[ A = \begin{pmatrix} 1 & -1 & 2 & 0 \\ 2 & -2 & 5 & 1 \\ 1 & -1 & 3 & 1 \end{pmatrix} \in M_{3 \times 4}(\nR). \] Hence write the second and fourth columns of \(A\) as combinations of its pivot columns.

title: Exercise (B2: Normal form of a rank-one matrix)
content:
Let \(A =  egin{pmatrix} 1 & -1 & 2 \ -2 & 2 & -4 \end{pmatrix} \in M_{2 	imes 3}(
R)\) . Find invertible \(Q \in M_2(
R)\) and \(P \in M_3(

title: Exercise (B3: Rank-one pieces)
content: Let \(A \in M_{m \times n}(F)\) . Use @thm-column-row-factorization to show that if \(\rank A = 1\) , then \(A = \x\y\tp\) for some non-zero \(\x \in F^m\) and \(\y \in F^n\) . Show that if \(\rank A = r \ge 1\) , then \(A\) is a sum of \(r\) matrices of rank \(1\) , and that it is not a sum of fewer than \(r\) matrices of rank \(1\) . Write \(\begin{pmatrix} 1 & 2 & 0 & 3 \\ 2 & 4 & 1 & 4 \\ 3 & 6 & 1 & 7 \end{pmatrix}\) as a sum of two rank-one matrices.

title: Exercise (C1: Frobenius’s rank inequality)
content: Let \(A \in M_{m \times n}(F)\) , \(B \in M_{n \times p}(F)\) and \(C \in M_{p \times q}(F)\) . Write \(N = \nul(A) \subseteq F^n\) , and let \(S \colon F^n \to F^m\) be \(S\y = A\y\) . Show that \(\col(AB) = \{ A\y : \y \in \col(B) \}\) , and deduce from Rank–Nullity for \(S|_{\col(B)}\) that \(\rank(AB) = \rank B - \dim(N \cap \col(B))\) . Show similarly that \(\rank(ABC) = \rank(BC) - \dim(N \cap \col(BC))\) . Prove that \(\col(BC) \subseteq \col(B)\) , and deduce Frobenius’s inequality \[ \rank(ABC) + \rank B \ge \rank(AB) + \rank(BC). \] Deduce Sylvester’s inequality for matrices from (c). Hint: for (d), look for a special choice of the middle factor.

title: Exercise (C2: Counting over \nF_2)
content:
Show that \(M_2(
F_2)\) contains exactly \(1\) matrix of rank \(0\) , \(6\) of rank \(2\) and \(9\) of rank \(1\) . Deduce the sizes of the equivalence classes of \(M_2(
F_2)\) . Compare with similarity: how many matrices of \(M_2(
F_2)\) are similar to \(I_2\) ? Is the class of \(I_2\) under equivalence a union of several similarity classes?

title: Proposition 3.8.2 (Rank as the size of the thinnest factorization)
content: Let \(A \in M_{m \times n}(F)\) be non-zero. Then \(\rank A\) is the smallest integer \(s \ge 1\) such that \(A = BD\) for some \(B \in M_{m \times s}(F)\) and \(D \in M_{s \times n}(F)\) .

title: Theorem 3.8.1 (Column–Row Factorization)
content: Let \(A \in M_{m \times n}(F)\) have rank \(r \ge 1\) , with pivot columns \(j_1 < \dots < j_r\) . Let \(C \in M_{m \times r}(F)\) be the matrix whose columns are the pivot columns \(\a_{j_1}, \dots, \a_{j_r}\) of \(A\) , and let \(R \in M_{r \times n}(F)\) consist of the first \(r\) rows of the reduced row echelon form of \(A\) , that is, its non-zero rows. Then \[ A = CR . \] Moreover, the columns of \(C\) are linearly independent and the rows of \(R\) are linearly independent.

title: Theorem 3.8.3 (Rank Normal Form)
content: Let \(V\) and \(W\) be finite-dimensional with \(\dim V = n\) and \(\dim W = m\) , and let \(T \colon V \to W\) be linear of rank \(r\) . Then there are bases \(\sB\) of \(V\) and \(\sC\) of \(W\) such that \(\mtx{T}{\sB}{\sC} = N_r\) . Every \(A \in M_{m \times n}(F)\) is equivalent to \(N_r\) , where \(r = \rank A\) . Two matrices \(A, B \in M_{m \times n}(F)\) are equivalent if and only if \(\rank A = \rank B\) .

title: Theorem 3.8.4 (Rank of a Composition)
content: Let \(T \colon V \to W\) and \(S \colon W \to U\) be linear, with \(V\) and \(W\) finite-dimensional. Then \[ \rank(ST) \le \min(\rank S, \rank T). \]

title: Theorem 3.8.5 (Sylvester’s Rank Inequality)
content: Let \(T \colon V \to W\) and \(S \colon W \to U\) be linear, with \(V\) and \(W\) finite-dimensional. Then \[ \rank(ST) \ge \rank S + \rank T - \dim W . \] In matrix form: for \(A \in M_{m \times n}(F)\) and \(B \in M_{n \times p}(F)\) , \(\rank(AB) \ge \rank A + \rank B - n\) .

title: Definition 3.9.2 (Coset)
content: Let \(U\) be a subspace of a vector space \(V\) , and let \(\v \in V\) . The coset of \(U\) through \(\v\) is the subset \[ \v + U \coloneqq \{ \v + \u : \u \in U \} \subseteq V . \] Any \(\w \in \v + U\) is called a representative of the coset.

title: Definition 3.9.1 (Product of vector spaces)
content: Let \(V_1, \dots, V_k\) be vector spaces over the same field \(F\) . Their product (or external direct sum ) is the Cartesian product ( @def-cartesian-product ) \[ V_1 \times \dots \times V_k = \{ (\v_1, \dots, \v_k) : \v_i \in V_i \text{ for each } i \}, \] with addition and scalar multiplication defined entrywise : for \(a \in F\) , \[ (\v_1, \dots, \v_k) + (\w_1, \dots, \w_k) \coloneqq (\v_1 + \w_1, \dots, \v_k + \w_k), \qquad a(\v_1, \dots, \v_k) \coloneqq (a\v_1, \dots, a\v_k). \]

title: Definition 3.9.3 (Quotient space)
content: Let \(U\) be a subspace of a vector space \(V\) over \(F\) . The quotient space \(V/U\) (read “ \(V\) modulo \(U\) ”) is the set of all cosets of \(U\) , \[ V/U \coloneqq \{ \v + U : \v \in V \}, \] with the operations \[ (\v + U) + (\w + U) \coloneqq (\v + \w) + U, \qquad a(\v + U) \coloneqq a\v + U \qquad (\v, \w \in V,\ a \in F). \] The quotient map is \(\pi \colon V \to V/U\) , \(\pi(\v) = \v + U\) .

content:
Use the First Isomorphism Theorem to show: \(
R^3/L \cong

content: Let \(U = \Span((1, 1, 1)) \subseteq \nR^3\) . Find a basis of \(\nR^3/U\) , and write \((2, 5, -1) + U\) in it.

R^5\) , what is \(\dim(
R^5/U)\) ? What is \(\dim(

Let \(T \colon

title: Exercise (B3: Matrices modulo scalars)
content: Let \(n \ge 1\) and \(S = \{ cI_n : c \in F \} \subseteq M_n(F)\) . Show that \(S\) is a subspace and find \(\dim(M_n(F)/S)\) . For \(n = 2\) , find a basis of \(M_2(F)/S\) . Show that \(A + S = B + S\) if and only if \(A - B\) is a scalar matrix, and decide whether \(\begin{pmatrix} 3 & 1 \\ 0 & 5 \end{pmatrix} + S = \begin{pmatrix} 1 & 1 \\ 0 & 3 \end{pmatrix} + S\) .

title: Exercise (C1: The dimension formula from isomorphisms)
content: Let \(U\) and \(W\) be finite-dimensional subspaces of a vector space \(V\) . Using @thm-second-isomorphism and @thm-dimension-quotient , prove that \(\dim(U + W) = \dim U + \dim W - \dim(U \cap W)\) . Give a second proof: apply Rank–Nullity to the addition map \(S \colon U \times W \to V\) , \(S(\u, \w) = \u + \w\) , after showing that \(\u \mapsto (\u, -\u)\) is an isomorphism from \(U \cap W\) onto \(\ker S\) .

title: Exercise (C2: The operator induced on a quotient)
content: Let \(V\) be finite-dimensional, \(T \in \cL(V)\) , and \(U\) a subspace with \(T\u \in U\) for every \(\u \in U\) . Prove that \(\bar T(\v + U) \coloneqq T\v + U\) is a well-defined linear operator on \(V/U\) . Let \((\u_1, \dots, \u_m)\) be a basis of \(U\) , extended to a basis \(\sB = (\u_1, \dots, \u_m, \w_1, \dots, \w_s)\) of \(V\) . Show that \[ [T]_{\sB} = \begin{pmatrix} A & B \\ 0 & D \end{pmatrix}, \] where \(A \in M_m(F)\) is the matrix of the restriction \(T|_U \colon U \to U\) in \((\u_1, \dots, \u_m)\) , \(D \in M_s(F)\) is the matrix of \(\bar T\) in \((\w_1 + U, \dots, \w_s + U)\) , and \(0\) is the \(s \times m\) zero matrix. Check (b) when \(T\) is differentiation on \(\nR[x]_{\le 2}\) , with \(U = \nR[x]_{\le 1}\) and \(\sB = (1, x, x^2)\) . Hint: for (a), apply @thm-quotient-universal-property to \(\pi \circ T\) .

title: Exercise (C3: Counting cosets over a finite field)
content: Let \(F = \nF_q\) be a finite field with \(q\) elements, \(V\) a vector space over \(F\) of dimension \(n\) , and \(U\) a subspace of dimension \(m\) . Show that \(\lvert V \rvert = q^n\) . Show that every coset \(\v + U\) has exactly \(\lvert U \rvert\) elements, and deduce \(\lvert V/U \rvert = q^{n - m}\) by counting. Check that (b) agrees with @thm-dimension-quotient .

title: Lemma 3.9.3 (When two cosets are equal)
content: Let \(U\) be a subspace of \(V\) . For \(\v, \w \in V\) , write \(\v \sim \w\) if \(\v - \w \in U\) . \(\sim\) is an equivalence relation on \(V\) , and the equivalence class of \(\v\) is the coset \(\v + U\) . \(\v + U = \w + U\) if and only if \(\v - \w \in U\) . Two cosets of \(U\) are either equal or disjoint, and every vector of \(V\) lies in exactly one coset.

title: Proposition 3.9.6 (A complement is a model of the quotient)
content: Let \(U\) be a subspace of \(V\) , and let \(W\) be a subspace with \(V = U \oplus W\) . Then the restriction of the quotient map, \(W \to V/U\) , \(\w \mapsto \w + U\) , is an isomorphism.

title: Theorem 3.9.1 (Dimension of a Product)
content: Let \(V_1, \dots, V_k\) be finite-dimensional vector spaces over \(F\) , and let \((\b_{i1}, \dots, \b_{in_i})\) be a basis of \(V_i\) for each \(i\) . Then the list of all vectors \(\iota_i(\b_{ij})\) , for \(i = 1, \dots, k\) and \(j = 1, \dots, n_i\) , is a basis of \(V_1 \times \dots \times V_k\) . In particular, \[ \dim(V_1 \times \dots \times V_k) = \dim V_1 + \dots + \dim V_k . \]

title: Theorem 3.9.5 (Dimension of a Quotient)
content: Let \(V\) be finite-dimensional and \(U\) a subspace of \(V\) . Then \(V/U\) is finite-dimensional and \[ \dim(V/U) = \dim V - \dim U . \] More precisely, if \((\u_1, \dots, \u_m, \w_1, \dots, \w_s)\) is a basis of \(V\) such that \((\u_1, \dots, \u_m)\) is a basis of \(U\) , then \((\w_1 + U, \dots, \w_s + U)\) is a basis of \(V/U\) .

title: Theorem 3.9.7 (First Isomorphism Theorem)
content: Let \(T \colon V \to W\) be a linear map, and let \(K = \ker T\) . Then the rule \[ \bar T \colon V/K \to W, \qquad \bar T(\v + K) = T\v \] defines a linear map, which is injective with \(\im \bar T = \im T\) , and satisfies \(\bar T \circ \pi = T\) . Hence \[ V/\ker T \cong \im T . \]

title: Theorem 3.9.2 (Internal and External Direct Sums)
content: Let \(U_1, \dots, U_k\) be subspaces of a vector space \(V\) , and let \[ S \colon U_1 \times \dots \times U_k \to V, \qquad S(\u_1, \dots, \u_k) = \u_1 + \dots + \u_k . \] Then \(S\) is linear with \(\im S = U_1 + \dots + U_k\) . It is injective if and only if the sum \(U_1 + \dots + U_k\) is direct. In that case \(S\) is an isomorphism from \(U_1 \times \dots \times U_k\) onto \(U_1 \oplus \dots \oplus U_k\) . Conversely, let \(V_1, \dots, V_k\) be vector spaces over \(F\) . Then the images \(\iota_i(V_i)\) are subspaces of \(V_1 \times \dots \times V_k\) , each isomorphic to \(V_i\) via \(\iota_i\) , and \[ V_1 \times \dots \times V_k = \iota_1(V_1) \oplus \dots \oplus \iota_k(V_k). \]

title: Theorem 3.9.4 (The Quotient Space Is a Vector Space)
content: Let \(U\) be a subspace of a vector space \(V\) over \(F\) . The addition and scalar multiplication in @def-quotient-space are well defined: the right-hand sides depend only on the cosets \(\v + U\) and \(\w + U\) , not on the representatives \(\v\) and \(\w\) . With these operations \(V/U\) is a vector space over \(F\) . Its zero vector is \(\0 + U = U\) , and the additive inverse of \(\v + U\) is \((-\v) + U\) . The quotient map \(\pi \colon V \to V/U\) is linear and surjective, and \(\ker \pi = U\) .

title: Theorem 3.9.10 (Universal Property of the Quotient)
content: Let \(U\) be a subspace of \(V\) , \(\pi \colon V \to V/U\) the quotient map, and \(T \colon V \to W\) a linear map. If \(U \subseteq \ker T\) , then there is exactly one linear map \(\bar T \colon V/U \to W\) with \(\bar T \circ \pi = T\) , namely \(\bar T(\v + U) = T\v\) . Its image is \(\im T\) , and it is injective if and only if \(U = \ker T\) . Conversely, if some function \(\bar T \colon V/U \to W\) satisfies \(\bar T \circ \pi = T\) , then \(U \subseteq \ker T\) .

title: Theorem 3.9.8 (Second Isomorphism Theorem)
content: Let \(U\) and \(W\) be subspaces of a vector space \(V\) . Then \(U \cap W\) is a subspace of \(U\) , \(W\) is a subspace of \(U + W\) , and \[ U/(U \cap W) \to (U + W)/W, \qquad \u + (U \cap W) \mapsto \u + W \] is a well-defined isomorphism. Hence \((U + W)/W \cong U/(U \cap W)\) .

title: Theorem 3.9.9 (Third Isomorphism Theorem)
content: Let \(U \subseteq W \subseteq V\) be subspaces. Then \(W/U = \{ \w + U : \w \in W \}\) is a subspace of \(V/U\) , and \[ (V/U)/(W/U) \to V/W, \qquad (\v + U) + W/U \mapsto \v + W \] is a well-defined isomorphism. Hence \((V/U)/(W/U) \cong V/W\) .

title: Corollary 3.10.2 (The matrix of a projection)
page: 3.10 Projections and the Trace of an Operator
content: Let \(V\) be finite-dimensional and \(P \in \cL(V)\) a projection with \(\rank P = r\) . Let \((\u_1, \dots, \u_r)\) be a basis of \(\im P\) and \((\w_1, \dots, \w_s)\) a basis of \(\ker P\) . Then \(\sB = (\u_1, \dots, \u_r, \w_1, \dots, \w_s)\) is a basis of \(V\) , and \[ [P]_{\sB} = \begin{pmatrix} I_r & 0 \\ 0 & 0 \end{pmatrix} = \diag(1, \dots, 1, 0, \dots, 0), \] with \(r\) ones.

title: Definition 3.10.1 (Projection)
page: 3.10 Projections and the Trace of an Operator
content: Let \(V\) be a vector space over \(F\) . An operator \(P \in \cL(V)\) is a projection if \[ P^2 = P, \] that is, \(P(P\v) = P\v\) for every \(\v \in V\) .

title: Definition 3.10.2 (Trace of an operator)
page: 3.10 Projections and the Trace of an Operator
content: Let \(V\) be a finite-dimensional vector space over \(F\) with \(\dim V \ge 1\) , and let \(T \in \cL(V)\) . The trace of \(T\) is \[ \tr T \coloneqq \tr [T]_{\sB}, \] where \(\sB\) is any basis of \(V\) . (For \(V = \{\0\}\) we set \(\tr T = 0\) .)

title: Example (Projecting onto a plane along a line)
page: 3.10 Projections and the Trace of an Operator
content: In \(\nR^3\) , let \(U = \{ (x, y, z) : x + y + z = 0 \}\) and \(L = \Span((1, 1, 1))\) , so that \(\nR^3 = U \oplus L\) by @exm-plane-line-direct-sum . Find the standard matrix of the projection \(P\) onto \(U\) along \(L\) , and check that it squares to itself.

title: Exercise (A1)
page: 3.10 Projections and the Trace of an Operator
content: Define a projection \(P \in \cL(V)\) , and state the correspondence between projections and direct sum decompositions. True or false: a projection is determined by its image. Justify your answer. True or false: an operator \(T\) on \(\nR^2\) with \(\im T\) the \(x\) -axis and \(\ker T\) the \(y\) -axis is a projection. Justify your answer. Explain why \(\tr T\) does not depend on the basis used to compute it. True or false: for every field \(F\) and every projection \(P\) on a finite-dimensional space over \(F\) , the integer \(\rank P\) can be recovered from \(\tr P \in F\) . Justify your answer. Where does the hypothesis “characteristic not \(2\) ” enter the proof of @thm-involution-decomposition ?

title: Exercise (B1: A projection in \nR^3)
page: 3.10 Projections and the Trace of an Operator
content: Let \(U = \{ (x, y, z) \in \nR^3 : x + y - z = 0 \}\) and \(L = \Span((1, 1, 1))\) . Show that \(\nR^3 = U \oplus L\) . Find the standard matrix \(A\) of the projection \(P\) onto \(U\) along \(L\) . Verify that \(A^2 = A\) , and that \(\tr A = \rank A\) .

title: Exercise (B2: The complementary projection)
page: 3.10 Projections and the Trace of an Operator
content: Let \(P \in \cL(V)\) be a projection. Prove that \(\id_V - P\) is a projection. Prove that \(\im(\id_V - P) = \ker P\) and \(\ker(\id_V - P) = \im P\) . Deduce that if \(P\) is the projection onto \(U\) along \(W\) , then \(\id_V - P\) is the projection onto \(W\) along \(U\) .

title: Exercise (B3: Traces of operators on matrices)
page: 3.10 Projections and the Trace of an Operator
content: Let \(\tau \colon M_n(F) \to M_n(F)\) , \(\tau(A) = A\tp\) . Show that \(\tr \tau = n \cdot 1\) . Fix \(B \in M_2(F)\) , and let \(L_B \colon M_2(F) \to M_2(F)\) , \(L_B(X) = BX\) . Show that \(\tr L_B = 2\tr B\) . Hint: use the basis of matrix units \(E_{ij}\) .

title: Exercise (C1: When is a sum of projections a projection?)
page: 3.10 Projections and the Trace of an Operator
content: Let \(F\) have characteristic not \(2\) , and let \(P, Q \in \cL(V)\) be projections. Prove that \(P + Q\) is a projection if and only if \(PQ = QP = 0\) . Show that (a) fails over \(\nF_2\) . Suppose \(V\) is finite-dimensional over \(\nR\) and \(P + Q\) is a projection. Deduce that \(\rank(P + Q) = \rank P + \rank Q\) . Hint: for (⇒) in (a), use the relation \(PQ + QP = 0\) together with \(P^2 = P\) .

title: Exercise (C2: The trace is the only trace-like functional)
page: 3.10 Projections and the Trace of an Operator
content: Let \(n \ge 1\) , and let \(\varphi \colon M_n(F) \to F\) be linear with \(\varphi(AB) = \varphi(BA)\) for all \(A, B \in M_n(F)\) . Using \(E_{ij}E_{jk} = E_{ik}\) and \(E_{jk}E_{ij} = 0\) for \(k \ne i\) , show that \(\varphi(E_{ik}) = 0\) whenever \(i \ne k\) . Show that \(\varphi(E_{ii}) = \varphi(E_{jj})\) for all \(i, j\) . Deduce that \(\varphi = c\,\tr\) for some \(c \in F\) , and conversely that every \(c\,\tr\) has the property.

title: Theorem 3.10.5 (Involutions Split the Space)
page: 3.10 Projections and the Trace of an Operator
content: Let \(F\) be a field of characteristic not \(2\) , \(V\) a vector space over \(F\) , and \(T \in \cL(V)\) with \(T^2 = \id_V\) . Then \[ V = E_{+} \oplus E_{-}, \] and the projection onto \(E_{+}\) along \(E_{-}\) is \(\frac12(\id_V + T)\) .

title: Theorem 3.10.1 (Projections and Direct Sums)
page: 3.10 Projections and the Trace of an Operator
content: Let \(V\) be a vector space. If \(P \in \cL(V)\) is a projection, then \[ V = \im P \oplus \ker P, \] \(P\) is the identity on \(\im P\) , and \(P\) is zero on \(\ker P\) . Conversely, suppose \(V = U \oplus W\) . Then there is exactly one operator \(P \in \cL(V)\) with \(P\u = \u\) for all \(\u \in U\) and \(P\w = \0\) for all \(\w \in W\) , namely \(P(\u + \w) = \u\) . It is a projection, with \(\im P = U\) and \(\ker P = W\) . It is called the projection onto \(U\) along \(W\) .

title: Theorem 3.10.4 (Trace of a Projection)
page: 3.10 Projections and the Trace of an Operator
content: Let \(V\) be a finite-dimensional vector space over \(F\) and \(P \in \cL(V)\) a projection. Then \[ \tr P = (\rank P) \cdot 1 \quad \text{in } F . \] If \(F\) has characteristic \(0\) , or characteristic \(p > \dim V\) , then \(\rank P\) is determined by \(\tr P\) : it is the unique integer \(r\) with \(0 \le r \le \dim V\) and \(r \cdot 1 = \tr P\) . In particular \(\rank P = \tr P\) for projections on real or complex spaces.

title: Theorem 3.10.3 (Properties of the Trace of an Operator)
page: 3.10 Projections and the Trace of an Operator
content: Let \(V\) be finite-dimensional with \(n = \dim V\) , let \(S, T \in \cL(V)\) and \(c \in F\) . Then \[ \tr(S + T) = \tr S + \tr T, \qquad \tr(cT) = c\,\tr T, \qquad \tr(ST) = \tr(TS), \qquad \tr \id_V = n \cdot 1 . \]

title: Corollary 4.1.4 (Dimension of the Dual Space)
page: 4.1 Linear Functionals and the Dual Space
content: Let \(V\) be a finite-dimensional vector space over \(F\) . Then \(V^{*}\) is finite-dimensional and \(\dim V^{*} = \dim V\) . In particular \(V^{*} \cong V\) .

title: Definition 4.1.3 (Dual Basis)
page: 4.1 Linear Functionals and the Dual Space
content: Let \(\sB = (\v_1, \dots, \v_n)\) be a basis of a finite-dimensional vector space \(V\) over \(F\) . The basis \((\varphi_1, \dots, \varphi_n)\) of \(V^{*}\) given by @thm-dual-basis , characterized by \(\varphi_i(\v_j) = \delta_{ij}\) , is the dual basis of \(\sB\) . We write it \(\sB^{*}\) .

title: Definition 4.1.2 (Dual Space)
page: 4.1 Linear Functionals and the Dual Space
content: Let \(V\) be a vector space over \(F\) . The dual space of \(V\) is the set of all linear functionals on \(V\) , \[ V^{*} \coloneqq \cL(V, F), \] with the pointwise operations \((\varphi + \psi)(\v) \coloneqq \varphi(\v) + \psi(\v)\) and \((c\varphi)(\v) \coloneqq c\,\varphi(\v)\) for \(\varphi, \psi \in V^{*}\) , \(c \in F\) and \(\v \in V\) .

title: Definition 4.1.1 (Linear Functional)
page: 4.1 Linear Functionals and the Dual Space
content: Let \(V\) be a vector space over \(F\) , and regard \(F\) as a vector space over itself. A linear functional on \(V\) is a linear map \(\varphi \colon V \to F\) . That is, for all \(\u, \v \in V\) and all \(c \in F\) , \[ \varphi(\u + \v) = \varphi(\u) + \varphi(\v), \qquad \varphi(c\v) = c\,\varphi(\v). \]

title: Example (The Dual Basis Is Read Off the Inverse Matrix)
page: 4.1 Linear Functionals and the Dual Space
content: Find the dual basis of \(\sB = ((1, 1), (1, -1))\) in \(\nR^2\) . More generally, let \(\sB = (\v_1, \dots, \v_n)\) be a basis of \(F^n\) , and let \(P = \begin{pmatrix} \v_1 & \cdots & \v_n \end{pmatrix}\) . Show that \(P\) is invertible and that the dual basis of \(\sB\) is \(\varphi_i(\x) = \r_i\x\) , where \(\r_i\) is the \(i\) -th row of \(P^{-1}\) .

page: 4.1 Linear Functionals and the Dual Space
content: Define a linear functional on a vector space \(V\) over \(F\) , and the dual space \(V^{*}\) . True or false: \(p \mapsto p(1)^2\) is a linear functional on \(\nR[x]\) . Justify your answer. page: 4.1 Linear Functionals and the Dual Space
content: Let \((\varphi_1, \varphi_2)\) be the dual basis of \(((1, 1), (1, -1))\) from @exm-dual-basis-inverse-rows . title: Exercise (C1: Functionals with the same kernel)
page: 4.1 Linear Functionals and the Dual Space
content: Let \(V\) be any vector space over \(F\) , and let \(\varphi, \psi \in V^{*}\) with \(\ker\varphi = \ker\psi\) . Prove that \(\psi = c\varphi\) for some \(c \in F\) . Is the converse true? Hint: if \(\varphi \neq 0\) , fix \(\u\) with \(\varphi(\u) = 1\) and consider \(\v - \varphi(\v)\u\) .

title: Exercise (C2: Functionals vanishing where others vanish)
page: 4.1 Linear Functionals and the Dual Space
content: Let \(V\) be a vector space over \(F\) , and let \(\varphi_1, \dots, \varphi_k, \psi \in V^{*}\) . Prove that if \(\ker\varphi_1 \cap \dots \cap \ker\varphi_k \subseteq \ker\psi\) , then \(\psi \in \Span(\varphi_1, \dots, \varphi_k)\) . Deduce that if \(V\) is finite-dimensional, then \((\varphi_1, \dots, \varphi_k)\) spans \(V^{*}\) if and only if \(\ker\varphi_1 \cap \dots \cap \ker\varphi_k = \{\0\}\) . Hint: for (a), consider the linear map \(T \colon V \to F^k\) , \(\v \mapsto (\varphi_1(\v), \dots, \varphi_k(\v))\) .

title: Exercise (C4: How large is F\lbrack x\rbrack^{*}?)
page: 4.1 Linear Functionals and the Dual Space
content: Let \(F^{\nN}\) be the space of sequences with entries in \(F\) . Prove that \(\Phi \colon F[x]^{*} \to F^{\nN}\) , \(\varphi \mapsto (\varphi(1), \varphi(x), \varphi(x^2), \dots)\) , is an isomorphism. Identify \(\Phi(\varphi_k)\) for the coordinate functionals \(\varphi_k\) of @prp-coordinate-functionals-do-not-span , and \(\Phi(\varepsilon_1)\) . Explain how @prp-coordinate-functionals-do-not-span matches @exm-sequence-standard-vectors . Hint: for surjectivity, remember that a polynomial has only finitely many non-zero coefficients.

title: Proposition 4.1.6 (The Coordinate Functionals Do Not Span F[x]^{*})
page: 4.1 Linear Functionals and the Dual Space
content: The functionals \(\varphi_k\) ( \(k \in \nN\) ) lie in \(F[x]^{*}\) and form a linearly independent set. But they do not span \(F[x]^{*}\) : the evaluation \(\varepsilon_1 \colon p \mapsto p(1)\) is not a linear combination of finitely many \(\varphi_k\) .

title: Proposition 4.1.2 (A Non-Zero Functional Is Surjective)
page: 4.1 Linear Functionals and the Dual Space
content: Let \(V\) be a vector space over \(F\) , and let \(\varphi \in V^{*}\) be non-zero . Then \(\varphi\) is surjective. If \(V\) is finite-dimensional, then \(\dim \ker\varphi = \dim V - 1\) .

title: Theorem 4.1.3 (The Dual Basis)
page: 4.1 Linear Functionals and the Dual Space
content: Let \(V\) be a finite-dimensional vector space over \(F\) , and let \(\sB = (\v_1, \dots, \v_n)\) be a basis of \(V\) . There are unique \(\varphi_1, \dots, \varphi_n \in V^{*}\) with \(\varphi_i(\v_j) = \delta_{ij}\) for all \(i, j\) . For every \(\v \in V\) , \(\varphi_i(\v)\) is the \(i\) -th entry of \(\coord{\v}{\sB}\) . The list \((\varphi_1, \dots, \varphi_n)\) is a basis of \(V^{*}\) . For every \(\v \in V\) and every \(\varphi \in V^{*}\) , \[ \v = \sum_{i=1}^{n} \varphi_i(\v)\,\v_i, \qquad \varphi = \sum_{i=1}^{n} \varphi(\v_i)\,\varphi_i . \]

title: Theorem 4.1.1 (Functionals on F^n Are Row Vectors)
page: 4.1 Linear Functionals and the Dual Space
content: For \(\a = (a_1, \dots, a_n) \in F^n\) , define \(\varphi_{\a} \colon F^n \to F\) by \[ \varphi_{\a}(\x) \coloneqq \a\tp\x = a_1x_1 + \dots + a_nx_n . \] Then \(\varphi_{\a} \in (F^n)^{*}\) . Every \(\varphi \in (F^n)^{*}\) equals \(\varphi_{\a}\) for exactly one \(\a\) , namely \(\a = (\varphi(\e_1), \dots, \varphi(\e_n))\) . The map \(F^n \to (F^n)^{*}\) , \(\a \mapsto \varphi_{\a}\) , is an isomorphism.

title: Theorem 4.1.5 (Functionals Separate Vectors)
page: 4.1 Linear Functionals and the Dual Space
content: Let \(V\) be a finite-dimensional vector space over \(F\) . If \(\v \in V\) and \(\v \neq \0\) , then there is \(\varphi \in V^{*}\) with \(\varphi(\v) = 1\) . If \(\v \in V\) satisfies \(\varphi(\v) = 0\) for every \(\varphi \in V^{*}\) , then \(\v = \0\) . It suffices that \(\varphi_i(\v) = 0\) for the functionals \(\varphi_i\) of one dual basis. For \(\u, \w \in V\) : \(\u = \w\) if and only if \(\varphi(\u) = \varphi(\w)\) for every \(\varphi \in V^{*}\) .

title: Definition 4.2.1 (Annihilator)
content: Let \(V\) be a vector space over \(F\) , and let \(S \subseteq V\) be any subset . The annihilator of \(S\) is \[ S^{0} \coloneqq \{ \varphi \in V^{*} : \varphi(\s) = 0 \text{ for all } \s \in S \}. \]

title: Example (The Equations of a Root Condition)
Example (An Annihilator as a Null Space)
content: Find a basis of \(U^{0}\) for \(U = \Span((1, 2, 0), (0, 1, 1)) \subseteq \nR^3\) , and check the dimension formula.

title: Example (First Annihilators)
content: For any vector space \(V\) , find \(\{\0\}^{0}\) , \(\varnothing^{0}\) and \(V^{0}\) . In \(M_2(F)\) , find the annihilator of the single matrix \(E_{11}\) . In \(\nR[x]_{\le 2}\) , find the annihilator of \(S = \{1, x\}\) .

title: Exercise (A1)
content: Define the annihilator \(S^{0}\) of a subset \(S\) of a vector space \(V\) . True or false: \(U^{0}\) is a subspace of \(V\) . Justify your answer. Let \(U\) be a \(2\) -dimensional subspace of \(\nR^5\) . What is \(\dim U^{0}\) ? For a finite-dimensional \(V\) , what are \(\{\0\}^{0}\) and \(V^{0}\) ? True or false: if \(U \subsetneq W\) are subspaces of a finite-dimensional \(V\) , then \(W^{0} \subsetneq U^{0}\) . Justify your answer. To compute \(U^{0}\) for \(U = \Span(\u_1, \dots, \u_m) \subseteq F^n\) , which matrix do you row reduce, and why?

title: Exercise (B1: Computing annihilators)
content: Let \(U = \Span((1, 2, 1, 0), (2, 4, 3, 1), (1, 2, 2, 1)) \subseteq \nR^4\) . Find a basis of \(U^{0}\) , and verify that \(\dim U + \dim U^{0} = 4\) . Let \(U = \{ p \in \nR[x]_{\le 3} : p(1) = p(-1) = 0 \}\) . Show that \(U^{0} = \Span(\varepsilon_1, \varepsilon_{-1})\) , where \(\varepsilon_c(p) = p(c)\) .

title: Exercise (B2: Equations of the symmetric matrices)
content: Let \(U = \{ A \in M_2(\nR) : A\tp = A \}\) . Find \(U^{0}\) , and verify the dimension formula.

title: Exercise (B3: The equations of a hyperplane)
content: Let \(V\) be a finite-dimensional vector space over \(F\) , and let \(\varphi \in V^{*}\) be non-zero. Prove that \((\ker\varphi)^{0} = \Span(\varphi)\) .

title: Exercise (C1: The intersection formula without counting)
content: Let \(U, W\) be subspaces of a vector space \(V\) over \(F\) , and let \(\varphi \in (U \cap W)^{0}\) . Suppose \(V\) is finite-dimensional. Construct \(\psi \in U^{0}\) and \(\chi \in W^{0}\) with \(\varphi = \psi + \chi\) , without using any dimension formula. Explain how to modify the construction when \(V\) is infinite-dimensional. Deduce that \((U \cap W)^{0} = U^{0} + W^{0}\) holds in every vector space. Hint: extend a basis of \(U \cap W\) to a basis of \(U\) and, separately, to a basis of \(W\) .

title: Exercise (C2: Equations of a double root)
content: Let \(U = \{ p \in \nR[x]_{\le 3} : p(1) = 0 \text{ and } p'(1) = 0 \}\) , and let \(\varepsilon_1(p) = p(1)\) and \(\eta_1(p) = p'(1)\) . Prove that \(U^{0} = \Span(\varepsilon_1, \eta_1)\) . Deduce that \(\psi(p) = p(0) - p(2) + 2p'(1)\) does not vanish on \(U\) .

title: Exercise (C3: Dual of a direct sum decomposition)
content: Let \(V\) be finite-dimensional with \(V = U \oplus W\) . Prove that \(V^{*} = U^{0} \oplus W^{0}\) . In \(\nR^2\) , let \(U = \Span((1, 0))\) and \(W = \Span((1, 1))\) . Write \(\psi(x, y) = x\) as \(\psi_U + \psi_W\) with \(\psi_U \in U^{0}\) and \(\psi_W \in W^{0}\) .

title: Proposition 4.2.1 (The Annihilator Is a Subspace)
content: Let \(V\) be a vector space over \(F\) , and let \(S \subseteq V\) . Then \(S^{0}\) is a subspace of \(V^{*}\) .

title: Theorem 4.2.3 (Properties of Annihilators)
content: Let \(V\) be a vector space over \(F\) . If \(S \subseteq T \subseteq V\) , then \(T^{0} \subseteq S^{0}\) . For every subset \(S \subseteq V\) , \(S^{0} = (\Span S)^{0}\) . For subspaces \(U, W\) of \(V\) , \((U + W)^{0} = U^{0} \cap W^{0}\) . If \(V\) is finite-dimensional , then for subspaces \(U, W\) of \(V\) , \((U \cap W)^{0} = U^{0} + W^{0}\) .

title: Theorem 4.2.2 (Dimension of the Annihilator)
content: Let \(V\) be a finite-dimensional vector space over \(F\) , and let \(U\) be a subspace of \(V\) . Then \[ \dim U + \dim U^{0} = \dim V . \] More precisely, if \((\u_1, \dots, \u_m, \v_{m+1}, \dots, \v_n)\) is a basis of \(V\) extending a basis \((\u_1, \dots, \u_m)\) of \(U\) , with dual basis \((\varphi_1, \dots, \varphi_n)\) , then \((\varphi_{m+1}, \dots, \varphi_n)\) is a basis of \(U^{0}\) .

title: Corollary 4.3.4 (The Annihilator of the Annihilator)
content: Let \(V\) be a finite-dimensional vector space over \(F\) , and let \(U\) be a subspace of \(V\) . Write \(U^{00} \coloneqq (U^{0})^{0} \subseteq V^{**}\) . Then \[ U^{00} = \ev_V(U) = \{ \ev_{\u} : \u \in U \}. \] So, under the identification \(\v \leftrightarrow \ev_{\v}\) , we have \(U^{00} = U\) . Equivalently, \[ U = \{ \v \in V : \varphi(\v) = 0 \text{ for every } \varphi \in U^{0} \}. \]

title: Corollary 4.3.3 (Every Basis of the Dual Is a Dual Basis)
content: Let \(V\) be a finite-dimensional vector space over \(F\) , and let \((\psi_1, \dots, \psi_n)\) be a basis of \(V^{*}\) . Then there is exactly one basis \((\v_1, \dots, \v_n)\) of \(V\) whose dual basis is \((\psi_1, \dots, \psi_n)\) , that is, with \[ \psi_i(\v_j) = \delta_{ij} \qquad \text{for all } i, j. \]

title: Corollary 4.3.5 (Subspaces Are Determined by Their Annihilators)
content: Let \(V\) be a finite-dimensional vector space, and let \(U\) and \(W\) be subspaces of \(V\) . Then \(U = W\) if and only if \(U^{0} = W^{0}\) .

title: Definition 4.3.1 (Double Dual and Evaluation Map)
content: Let \(V\) be a vector space over \(F\) . The double dual of \(V\) is \(V^{**} \coloneqq (V^{*})^{*}\) , the space of linear functionals on \(V^{*}\) . For \(\v \in V\) , evaluation at \(\v\) is the function \[ \ev_{\v} \colon V^{*} \to F, \qquad \ev_{\v}(\varphi) \coloneqq \varphi(\v). \] The evaluation map of \(V\) is \[ \ev_V \colon V \to V^{**}, \qquad \v \mapsto \ev_{\v}. \] When only one space is in play we write \(\ev\) for \(\ev_V\) .

title: Example (A Basis With Prescribed Dual Basis)
content: On \(V = \nR[x]_{\le 2}\) , consider the functionals \[ \psi_1(p) = p(0), \qquad \psi_2(p) = p(1), \qquad \psi_3(p) = p'(1). \] Show that \((\psi_1, \psi_2, \psi_3)\) is a basis of \(V^{*}\) , and find the basis \((p_1, p_2, p_3)\) of \(V\) whose dual basis it is.

title: Example (Evaluation in Three Spaces)
content: Let \(V = F^n\) . Describe \(\ev_{\x}\) for \(\x \in F^n\) in terms of row vectors. Let \(V = \nR[x]_{\le 2}\) , and let \((\varphi_0, \varphi_1, \varphi_2)\) be the dual basis of \((1, x, x^2)\) , so that \(\varphi_k(p)\) is the coefficient of \(x^k\) in \(p\) ( @exm-dual-basis-polynomials ). Compute \(\ev_{x^2}\) on \(\varphi_0, \varphi_1, \varphi_2\) and on the functional \(\varepsilon_3(p) = p(3)\) . Which element of \(V^{**}\) is \(\ev_{x^2}\) ? Describe \(\ev_{\0}\) , and the evaluation map of \(V = \{\0\}\) .

title: Example (A Functional on F\lbrack x\rbrack^{*} That Is Not an Evaluation)
content: Let \(\varphi_k \in F[x]^{*}\) ( \(k \in \nN\) ) be the coordinate functionals, \(\varphi_k(p) =\) the coefficient of \(x^k\) in \(p\) , and let \(\varepsilon_1(p) = p(1)\) , as in @prp-coordinate-functionals-do-not-span . Show that there is \(\theta \in F[x]^{**}\) with \(\theta \neq \ev_p\) for every \(p \in F[x]\) .

content:
Let \(\psi_1(x, y) = 2x + y\) and \(\psi_2(x, y) = x + y\) on \(

title: Exercise (B2: U^{00} = U for a line)
content: Let \(U = \Span\bigl((1, 2, -1)\bigr) \subseteq \nR^3\) . Find a basis of \(U^{0}\) . Find all \(\v \in \nR^3\) with \(\varphi(\v) = 0\) for every \(\varphi \in U^{0}\) , and check that the answer is \(U\) . Hence verify that \(U^{00} = \ev(U)\) , and confirm the dimension count.

title: Exercise (B3: Recognizing an evaluation)
content: Let \(V = \nR[x]_{\le 2}\) , with the coefficient functionals \(\varphi_0, \varphi_1, \varphi_2\) of @exm-evaluation-map . Let \(\theta \in V^{**}\) be the linear functional with \(\theta(\varphi_0) = 1\) , \(\theta(\varphi_1) = -3\) , \(\theta(\varphi_2) = 2\) . Find \(p \in V\) with \(\theta = \ev_p\) . Hence compute \(\theta(\varepsilon_1)\) and \(\theta(\psi)\) , where \(\varepsilon_1(q) = q(1)\) and \(\psi(q) = q'(0)\) .

title: Exercise (C1: Subspaces of V and of V^{*})
content: Let \(V\) be a finite-dimensional vector space over \(F\) . Prove that \(U \mapsto U^{0}\) is a bijection from the set of subspaces of \(V\) to the set of subspaces of \(V^{*}\) , and that it reverses inclusions in both directions: \(U \subseteq W\) if and only if \(W^{0} \subseteq U^{0}\) . Hint: for surjectivity, given a subspace \(X \subseteq V^{*}\) , consider \(U = \{ \v \in V : \varphi(\v) = 0 \text{ for all } \varphi \in X \}\) .

title: Exercise (C2: Spans cut out by equations)
content: Let \(V\) be finite-dimensional and \(S \subseteq V\) any subset. Prove that \(\{ \v \in V : \varphi(\v) = 0 \text{ for every } \varphi \in S^{0} \} = \Span(S)\) . Deduce: a vector \(\v\) lies in \(\Span(S)\) if and only if every functional that vanishes on \(S\) vanishes at \(\v\) . Show by an example that (a) can fail if “ \(\Span(S)\) ” is replaced by “ \(S\) ”.

title: Exercise (C3: Where finite dimension is needed)
content: Let \(V = F[x]\) , let \(\varphi_k\) and \(\varepsilon_1\) be as in @exm-evaluation-not-surjective , and let \(X = \Span\{ \varphi_k : k \in \nN \} \subseteq V^{*}\) . Show that \(\{ p \in F[x] : \varphi(p) = 0 \text{ for all } \varphi \in X \} = \{0\}\) . Deduce that \(X \neq U^{0}\) for every subspace \(U\) of \(F[x]\) . So the map \(U \mapsto U^{0}\) of @exr-double-dual-c1 is not surjective for \(F[x]\) . Which step of the solution of @exr-double-dual-c1 fails here?

title: Theorem 4.3.2 (The Double Dual Isomorphism)
content: Let \(V\) be a finite-dimensional vector space over \(F\) . Then the evaluation map \(\ev_V \colon V \to V^{**}\) is an isomorphism. Moreover, if \(\sB = (\v_1, \dots, \v_n)\) is a basis of \(V\) with dual basis \(\sB^{*} = (\varphi_1, \dots, \varphi_n)\) , then \((\ev_{\v_1}, \dots, \ev_{\v_n})\) is the dual basis of \(\sB^{*}\) .

title: Theorem 4.3.1 (The Evaluation Map Is Linear and Injective)
content: Let \(V\) be any vector space over \(F\) . Then the evaluation map \(\ev_V \colon V \to V^{**}\) is linear and injective.

title: Corollary 4.4.5 (Injective and Surjective Swap Under Duality)
page: 4.4 The Dual Map and the Transpose
content: Let \(V\) and \(W\) be finite-dimensional vector spaces over \(F\) , and \(T \in \cL(V, W)\) . Then: \(T\) is surjective if and only if \(T'\) is injective; \(T\) is injective if and only if \(T'\) is surjective.

title: Corollary 4.4.4 (Rank of the Dual Map)
page: 4.4 The Dual Map and the Transpose
content: Let \(V\) and \(W\) be finite-dimensional vector spaces over \(F\) , and \(T \in \cL(V, W)\) . Then \(\rank T' = \rank T\) . For every \(A \in M_{m \times n}(F)\) , \(\rank A\tp = \rank A\) . Equivalently, \(\dim \row(A) = \dim \col(A)\) : row rank equals column rank .

title: Definition 4.4.1 (Dual Map)
page: 4.4 The Dual Map and the Transpose
content: Let \(V\) and \(W\) be vector spaces over \(F\) , and let \(T \in \cL(V, W)\) . The dual map of \(T\) is the map \[ T' \colon W^{*} \to V^{*}, \qquad T'(\psi) \coloneqq \psi T = \psi \circ T . \] That is, \((T'\psi)(\v) = \psi(T\v)\) for every \(\psi \in W^{*}\) and every \(\v \in V\) .

title: Exercise (A1)

title: Exercise (B3: The transpose of a product, again)
page: 4.4 The Dual Map and the Transpose
content: Let \(A \in M_{m \times n}(F)\) and \(B \in M_{n \times p}(F)\) . Using \(T_AT_B = T_{AB}\) (Chapter 3, §6), @thm-dual-map-properties (b) and @thm-matrix-of-dual-map , give a new proof that \((AB)\tp = B\tp A\tp\) .

title: Exercise (C1: The Fredholm alternative)
page: 4.4 The Dual Map and the Transpose
content: Let \(V, W\) be finite-dimensional, \(T \in \cL(V, W)\) and \(\w \in W\) . Prove that \(T\v = \w\) has a solution \(\v \in V\) if and only if \(\psi(\w) = 0\) for every \(\psi \in \ker T'\) . Deduce: for \(A \in M_{m \times n}(F)\) and \(\b \in F^m\) , the system \(A\x = \b\) is consistent if and only if \(\y\tp\b = 0\) for every \(\y \in F^m\) with \(A\tp\y = \0\) . Let \(A = \begin{pmatrix} 1 & 1 \\ 1 & 2 \\ 1 & 3 \end{pmatrix}\) . Find a single linear condition on \(\b = (b_1, b_2, b_3) \in \nR^3\) that is equivalent to consistency of \(A\x = \b\) . Hint: for (a), combine @thm-kernel-image-dual-map with the description of a subspace by its annihilator in the previous section.

title: Exercise (C2: Invariant subspaces and annihilators)
page: 4.4 The Dual Map and the Transpose
content: Let \(V\) be finite-dimensional, \(T \in \cL(V)\) , and \(U\) a subspace of \(V\) . Recall that \(U\) is \(T\) -invariant if \(T\u \in U\) for every \(\u \in U\) . Prove that \(U\) is \(T\) -invariant if and only if \(U^{0}\) is \(T'\) -invariant.

title: Exercise (C3: Duality without finite dimension)
page: 4.4 The Dual Map and the Transpose
content: Let \(V\) and \(W\) be arbitrary vector spaces over \(F\) , and \(T \in \cL(V, W)\) . Prove that if \(T\) is surjective, then \(T'\) is injective. Prove that if \(T\) is injective, then \(T'\) is surjective. Check (b) on \(S \colon F[x] \to F[x]\) , \(S(p) = xp\) , from @exm-dual-map-examples (c): given \(\varphi \in F[x]^{*}\) , find \(\psi\) with \(S'\psi = \varphi\) . Is \(S'\) injective? Hint: for (b), use @thm-basis-extension-general in \(W\) .

title: Theorem 4.4.1 (Properties of the Dual Map)
page: 4.4 The Dual Map and the Transpose
content: Let \(U, V, W\) be vector spaces over \(F\) . For \(S, T \in \cL(V, W)\) and \(a, b \in F\) , \((aS + bT)' = aS' + bT'\) . For \(T \in \cL(U, V)\) and \(S \in \cL(V, W)\) , \((ST)' = T'S'\) . \((\id_V)' = \id_{V^{*}}\) . If \(T \in \cL(V, W)\) is invertible, then \(T'\) is invertible and \((T')^{-1} = (T^{-1})'\) .

title: Theorem 4.4.6 (The Evaluation Map Is Natural)
page: 4.4 The Dual Map and the Transpose
content: Let \(V\) and \(W\) be vector spaces over \(F\) , and let \(T \in \cL(V, W)\) . Then \[ T''\,\ev_V = \ev_W\,T . \] That is, \(T''(\ev_{\v}) = \ev_{T\v}\) for every \(\v \in V\) . If \(V\) and \(W\) are finite-dimensional, then \(T'' = \ev_W\,T\,\ev_V^{-1}\) .

title: Theorem 4.4.3 (Kernel and Image of the Dual Map)
page: 4.4 The Dual Map and the Transpose
content: Let \(V\) and \(W\) be vector spaces over \(F\) , and let \(T \in \cL(V, W)\) . \(\ker T' = (\im T)^{0}\) . If \(V\) and \(W\) are finite-dimensional, then \(\im T' = (\ker T)^{0}\) .

title: Theorem 4.4.2 (The Matrix of the Dual Map Is the Transpose)
page: 4.4 The Dual Map and the Transpose
content: Let \(V\) and \(W\) be finite-dimensional vector spaces over \(F\) , with ordered bases \(\sB\) of \(V\) and \(\sC\) of \(W\) , and let \(\sB^{*}\) and \(\sC^{*}\) be their dual bases. For every \(T \in \cL(V, W)\) , \[ \mtx{T'}{\sC^{*}}{\sB^{*}} = \left(\mtx{T}{\sB}{\sC}\right)\tp . \]

title: Definition 4.5.1 (Codimension)
content: Let \(U\) be a subspace of a vector space \(V\) over \(F\) . If \(V/U\) is finite-dimensional, the codimension of \(U\) in \(V\) is \[ \codim U \coloneqq \dim(V/U) . \] If \(V/U\) is infinite-dimensional, we say that \(U\) has infinite codimension .

title: Definition 4.5.2 (Hyperplane)
content: A hyperplane in \(V\) is a subspace \(H\) of \(V\) of codimension exactly \(1\) , that is, with \(\dim(V/H) = 1\) .

title: Exercise (B2: Functionals with the same kernel)
content: Let \(V\) be a vector space over \(F\) , of any dimension, and let \(\varphi, \psi \in V^{*}\) be non-zero. Prove that \(\ker\varphi = \ker\psi\) if and only if \(\psi = c\varphi\) for some non-zero \(c \in F\) . ( @exr-linear-functionals-c1 proved (⇒) by a different route; here use the hyperplane decomposition.) Hint: the remark after @thm-hyperplane-kernel-functional .

title: Exercise (B3: Dimension computations)
content: Let \(\dim V = 7\) and \(\dim U = 3\) . Find \(\dim U^{*}\) , \(\dim(V^{*}/U^{0})\) , \(\dim(V/U)^{*}\) and \(\codim U\) . In \(V = F[x]_{\le 3}\) , let \(U = \{ p : p(0) = p(1) = 0 \}\) . Using the map \(T \colon V \to F^2\) , \(T(p) = (p(0), p(1))\) , find \(\codim U\) and \(\dim U\) , and write \(U\) as an intersection of two hyperplanes. Hence find a basis of \(U^{0}\) consisting of evaluation functionals.

title: Exercise (C1: Subspaces of finite codimension are intersections of hyperplanes)
content: Let \(V\) be a vector space over \(F\) , of any dimension, and let \(U\) be a subspace of finite codimension \(k \ge 1\) . Prove that there are non-zero \(\varphi_1, \dots, \varphi_k \in U^{0}\) with \(U = \ker\varphi_1 \cap \dots \cap \ker\varphi_k\) . Deduce that \(U\) is an intersection of \(k\) hyperplanes. Prove that \(U\) is not an intersection of fewer than \(k\) hyperplanes. Hint: for (a), take a dual basis of \((V/U)^{*}\) ; for (b), consider the map \(V \to F^m\) , \(\v \mapsto (\varphi_1(\v), \dots, \varphi_m(\v))\) .

title: Exercise (C2: Complements and a choice of copy of U^{*})
content: Let \(V\) be finite-dimensional, and let \(U, W\) be subspaces with \(V = U \oplus W\) . Prove that \(V^{*} = U^{0} \oplus W^{0}\) without using @thm-annihilator-properties (d). (This is @exr-annihilators-c3 (a), which used it.) Deduce that the restriction map \(\rho \colon V^{*} \to U^{*}\) restricts to an isomorphism \(W^{0} \to U^{*}\) . In \(\nR^2\) , let \(U = \Span(\e_1)\) , \(W_1 = \Span(\e_2)\) and \(W_2 = \Span((1, 1))\) . Find \(W_1^{0}\) and \(W_2^{0}\) , and find the element of each that restricts to the functional \(\xi \in U^{*}\) with \(\xi(\e_1) = 1\) . Conclude that the copy of \(U^{*}\) inside \(V^{*}\) depends on the complement.

title: Theorem 4.5.2 (Dual of a Quotient)
content: Let \(V\) be a vector space over \(F\) , of any dimension, let \(U\) be a subspace, and let \(\pi \colon V \to V/U\) be the quotient map. Then the dual map \[ \pi' \colon (V/U)^{*} \to V^{*}, \qquad \pi'(\psi) = \psi \circ \pi , \] is injective, and its image is \(U^{0}\) . Hence \(\pi'\) is an isomorphism from \((V/U)^{*}\) onto \(U^{0}\) , and \((V/U)^{*} \cong U^{0}\) .

title: Theorem 4.5.1 (Dual of a Subspace)
content: Let \(V\) be a vector space over \(F\) , of any dimension, and let \(U\) be a subspace of \(V\) . The restriction map \(\rho \colon V^{*} \to U^{*}\) , \(\rho(\varphi) = \varphi|_U\) , is linear and surjective, and \(\ker \rho = U^{0}\) . Hence \[ V^{*}/U^{0} \to U^{*}, \qquad \varphi + U^{0} \mapsto \varphi|_U \] is a well-defined isomorphism, and \(U^{*} \cong V^{*}/U^{0}\) .

title: Theorem 4.5.3 (Hyperplanes Are Kernels of Functionals)
content: Let \(V\) be a vector space over \(F\) , of any dimension, and let \(H\) be a subspace of \(V\) . Then \(H\) is a hyperplane if and only if \(H = \ker \varphi\) for some non-zero \(\varphi \in V^{*}\) .

title: Corollary 4.6.6 (Same solutions, same row space)
content: Let \(A \in M_{m \times n}(F)\) and \(B \in M_{p \times n}(F)\) . Then \(\nul(A) = \nul(B)\) if and only if \(\row(A) = \row(B)\) .

title: Example (Equations for a plane in \nR^4)
content: Let \(U = \Span(\u_1, \u_2) \subseteq \nR^4\) , where \(\u_1 = (1, 1, 0, 1)\) and \(\u_2 = (0, 1, 1, 1)\) . Find a system of linear equations whose solution set is \(U\) .

title: Example (An intersection computed from equations)
content: In \(\nR^4\) , let \(U = \Span((1, 0, 1, 2), (0, 1, 1, 1))\) and \(W = \Span((1, 1, 0, 1), (1, 3, 0, 1))\) , as in @exm-intersection-by-elimination . Find \(U \cap W\) by first finding equations for \(U\) and for \(W\) .

content: Let \(U = \{ \x \in \nR^4 : x_1 + x_2 - x_3 + 2x_4 = 0, \ \ 2x_1 + 2x_2 + x_3 + x_4 = 0 \}\) . Find a basis of \(U\) . Run the parametric-to-implicit algorithm on your basis, and check that the resulting equations have the same solution set as the given ones, by comparing row spaces.

title: Exercise (C1: Avoiding finitely many subspaces)
content: Let \(F\) be an infinite field, \(V\) a vector space over \(F\) with \(1 \le \dim V = n < \infty\) , and \(U_1, \dots, U_k\) proper subspaces of \(V\) . Prove that for each \(i\) there is a non-zero \(\varphi_i \in V^{*}\) with \(U_i \subseteq \ker\varphi_i\) . Show that \(t \mapsto \varphi_i(\v(t))\) is given by a non-zero polynomial of degree at most \(n - 1\) . Deduce that some vector of \(V\) lies in none of \(U_1, \dots, U_k\) . In other words, \(V\) is not a union of finitely many proper subspaces. title: Lemma 4.6.1 (A subspace is cut out by its annihilator)
content: Let \(V\) be a finite-dimensional vector space and \(U\) a subspace. For \(\v \in V\) , \[ \v \in U \quad \iff \quad \varphi(\v) = 0 \text{ for every } \varphi \in U^{0} . \] If \((\varphi_1, \dots, \varphi_k)\) is a basis of \(U^{0}\) , then \(U = \ker\varphi_1 \cap \dots \cap \ker\varphi_k\) .

title: Proposition 4.6.4 (Cosets as intersections of affine hyperplanes)
content: Let \(U\) be a subspace of \(F^n\) of dimension \(k < n\) , and let \(\p \in F^n\) . Let \(A \in M_{(n-k) \times n}(F)\) be as in @thm-subspace-is-solution-set (a), with rows \(\a_1\tp, \dots, \a_{n-k}\tp\) . Then \[ \p + U = \{ \x \in F^n : A\x = A\p \} = \bigcap_{i=1}^{n-k} \{ \x : \a_i\tp\x = \a_i\tp\p \}, \] an intersection of \(n - k\) affine hyperplanes.

title: Theorem 4.6.7 (Independent Functionals)
content: Let \(V\) be a vector space over \(F\) , of any dimension, and let \(\varphi_1, \dots, \varphi_k \in V^{*}\) . The following are equivalent: \((\varphi_1, \dots, \varphi_k)\) is linearly independent in \(V^{*}\) ; \(\Phi \colon V \to F^k\) is surjective; \(\ker\varphi_1 \cap \dots \cap \ker\varphi_k\) has codimension exactly \(k\) .

title: Theorem 4.6.3 (Correctness of the Conversion)
content: Let \(\v_1, \dots, \v_p \in F^n\) , \(U = \Span(\v_1, \dots, \v_p)\) , and let \(M\) and \(A\) be as in the algorithm. Then \(\nul(A) = U\) , and \(A\) has exactly \(d = n - \dim U\) rows, which are linearly independent.

title: Theorem 4.6.5 (The Row Space Is the Annihilator of the Null Space)
content: Let \(A \in M_{m \times n}(F)\) . Identifying a row vector \(\a\tp \in M_{1 \times n}(F)\) with the functional \(\varphi_{\a} \in (F^n)^{*}\) , \[ \{ \varphi_{\a} : \a\tp \in \row(A) \} = \nul(A)^{0} . \] Consequently \(\dim \row(A) + \dim \nul(A) = n\) .

title: Theorem 4.6.2 (Every Subspace Is a Solution Set)
content: Let \(U\) be a subspace of \(F^n\) with \(\dim U = k\) . There is a matrix \(A \in M_{(n-k) \times n}(F)\) with \(U = \nul(A)\) . One may take as rows of \(A\) the vectors \(\a_1\tp, \dots, \a_{n-k}\tp\) for any \(\a_i \in F^n\) such that \((\varphi_{\a_1}, \dots, \varphi_{\a_{n-k}})\) is a basis of \(U^{0}\) . If \(B \in M_{m \times n}(F)\) and \(\nul(B) = U\) , then \(m \ge n - k\) . So \(U\) is the solution set of a homogeneous system of exactly \(n - k = \codim U\) equations, and of no system with fewer. (When \(k = n\) , that is \(U = F^n\) , this is the empty system, with no equations.)

title: Corollary 5.1.4 (Distinct Roots Give a Product of Linear Factors)
content: Let \(F\) be a field, \(f \in F[x]\) , and let \(c_1, \dots, c_k \in F\) be distinct roots of \(f\) , with \(k \ge 1\) . Then \[ (x - c_1)(x - c_2) \cdots (x - c_k) \mid f . \] Consequently, if \(f \neq 0\) , then \(k \le \deg f\) : a non-zero polynomial of degree \(n\) has at most \(n\) distinct roots in \(F\) .

title: Definition 5.1.1 (Divisibility, Associates)
content: Let \(F\) be a field and \(f, g \in F[x]\) . We say \(g\) divides \(f\) over \(F\) , and write \(g \mid f\) , if there exists \(h \in F[x]\) with \(f = gh\) . Then \(g\) is a divisor (or factor ) of \(f\) , and \(f\) is a multiple of \(g\) . We write \(g \nmid f\) if \(g\) does not divide \(f\) . We say \(f\) and \(g\) are associates if \(f = cg\) for some non-zero constant \(c \in F\) .

title: Example (Long Division with a Non-Monic Divisor)
content: In \(\nQ[x]\) , divide \(f = 2x^4 - 3x^3 + x^2 + 4x - 1\) by \(g = 2x^2 - x + 3\) with remainder.

title: Exercise (A1)
content: State the theorem on division with remainder in \(F[x]\) , including every hypothesis. Determine whether the following statement is true: “for every field \(F\) and all \(f, g \in F[x]\) , if \(f \mid g\) and \(g \mid f\) , then \(f = g\) .” Justify your answer. title: Exercise (C2: Remainders on Division by a Quadratic)
content: Let \(F\) be a field, \(f \in F[x]\) and \(a, b \in F\) . Suppose \(a \neq b\) . Prove that the remainder of \(f\) on division by \((x - a)(x - b)\) is \[ r = f(a)\,\frac{x - b}{a - b} + f(b)\,\frac{x - a}{b - a} , \] where \(\frac{x - b}{a - b}\) means \((a - b)^{-1}(x - b)\) . Now let \(a = b\) . Write \(f = (x - a)h + f(a)\) by @thm-remainder-theorem . Prove that the remainder of \(f\) on division by \((x - a)^2\) is \(h(a)(x - a) + f(a)\) . title: Proposition 5.1.2 (Rules for Divisibility)
content: Let \(F\) be a field and \(f, g, h \in F[x]\) . If \(f \mid g\) and \(g \mid h\) , then \(f \mid h\) . If \(h \mid f\) and \(h \mid g\) , then \(h \mid af + bg\) for all \(a, b \in F[x]\) . If \(g \mid f\) and \(f \neq 0\) , then \(\deg g \le \deg f\) . \(f \mid g\) and \(g \mid f\) if and only if \(f\) and \(g\) are associates or both are \(0\) . In particular, if \(f \mid g\) , \(g \mid f\) , and \(f, g\) are both monic, then \(f = g\) . If \(g \neq 0\) , then \(g \mid f\) if and only if the remainder of \(f\) on division by \(g\) is \(0\) .

title: Theorem 5.1.1 (Polynomial Division with Remainder)
content: Let \(F\) be a field, and let \(f, g \in F[x]\) with \(g \neq 0\) . Then there exist unique polynomials \(q, r \in F[x]\) such that \[ f = qg + r \qquad \text{and} \qquad \deg r < \deg g . \]

title: Theorem 5.1.5 (Values Determine a Polynomial)
content: Let \(F\) be a field and \(p, q \in F[x]\) . Let \(n \in \nN\) with \(\deg p \le n\) and \(\deg q \le n\) . If \(p(c) = q(c)\) for at least \(n + 1\) distinct elements \(c \in F\) , then \(p = q\) . If \(F\) is infinite and \(p(c) = q(c)\) for every \(c \in F\) , then \(p = q\) .

title: Theorem 5.1.3 (Remainder Theorem and Factor Theorem)
content: Let \(F\) be a field, \(f \in F[x]\) and \(c \in F\) . The remainder of \(f\) on division by \(x - c\) is the constant \(f(c)\) . \(c\) is a root of \(f\) if and only if \(x - c \mid f\) .

title: Corollary 5.2.4 (Bézout’s Identity for Polynomials)
content: Let \(F\) be a field and \(f, g \in F[x]\) . Then there exist \(a, b \in F[x]\) with \[ \gcd(f, g) = af + bg . \]

title: Definition 5.2.3 (Coprime Polynomials)
content: Let \(F\) be a field. Polynomials \(f, g \in F[x]\) are coprime (or relatively prime ) over \(F\) if \(\gcd(f, g) = 1\) .

title: Definition 5.2.2 (Greatest Common Divisor)
content: Let \(F\) be a field and \(f, g \in F[x]\) . If \(f\) and \(g\) are not both zero , the greatest common divisor \(\gcd(f, g)\) is the unique monic polynomial \(d \in F[x]\) with \[ \langle f, g \rangle = \langle d \rangle . \] We set \(\gcd(0, 0) = 0\) .

title: Definition 5.2.1 (Ideal of F\lbrack x\rbrack)
content: Let \(F\) be a field. A subset \(I \subseteq F[x]\) is an ideal of \(F[x]\) if \(I\) is non-empty ; \(f + g \in I\) for all \(f, g \in I\) ; \(hf \in I\) for all \(f \in I\) and every \(h \in F[x]\) . For \(f_1, \dots, f_k \in F[x]\) , write \[ \langle f_1, \dots, f_k \rangle \coloneqq \{ a_1 f_1 + \dots + a_k f_k : a_1, \dots, a_k \in F[x] \} . \] In particular \(\langle p \rangle = \{ hp : h \in F[x] \}\) is the set of all multiples of \(p\) .

title: Definition 5.2.4 (Least Common Multiple)
content: Let \(F\) be a field and \(f, g \in F[x]\) . The least common multiple \(\operatorname{lcm}(f, g)\) is the monic generator of the ideal \(\langle f \rangle \cap \langle g \rangle\) if this ideal is non-zero, and \(0\) otherwise.

title: Exercise (B3: The gcd of x^m - 1 and x^n - 1)
content: Let \(F\) be a field. For integers \(m, n \ge 0\) , not both zero, let \(\gcd(m, n)\) denote the largest positive integer dividing both. For \(m \ge n \ge 1\) , verify that \(x^m - 1 = x^{m-n}(x^n - 1) + (x^{m-n} - 1)\) . Prove that \(\gcd(x^m - 1, x^n - 1) = x^{\gcd(m, n)} - 1\) in \(F[x]\) for all \(m, n \ge 0\) not both zero, where \(x^0 - 1 = 0\) . Hence compute \(\gcd(x^{12} - 1, x^{18} - 1)\) . Hint for (b): @thm-euclidean-algorithm , run on the exponents.

title: Exercise (C1: Polynomials Vanishing on a Set)
content: Let \(F\) be a field and \(S \subseteq F\) non-empty. Put \(I(S) = \{ f \in F[x] : f(s) = 0 \text{ for all } s \in S \}\) . Prove that \(I(S)\) is an ideal of \(F[x]\) . Suppose \(S = \{ s_1, \dots, s_k \}\) is finite, with the \(s_i\) distinct. Prove that \(I(S) = \langle (x - s_1) \cdots (x - s_k) \rangle\) . Suppose \(S\) is infinite. Prove that \(I(S) = \{0\}\) . Deduce from (b) and @exr-division-c3 that \(I(\nF_p) = \langle x^p - x \rangle\) for every prime \(p\) .

title: Exercise (C3: gcd Times lcm)
content: Let \(F\) be a field and \(f, g \in F[x]\) monic . Put \(d = \gcd(f, g)\) and write \(f = d f_1\) , \(g = d g_1\) with \(f_1, g_1 \in F[x]\) . Prove that \(\gcd(f_1, g_1) = 1\) . Prove that \(m = d f_1 g_1\) is a monic common multiple of \(f\) and \(g\) that divides every common multiple of \(f\) and \(g\) . Deduce that \(\operatorname{lcm}(f, g) = d f_1 g_1\) , and hence \(\gcd(f, g) \cdot \operatorname{lcm}(f, g) = fg\) . Show by an example in \(\nQ[x]\) that the formula in (c) fails if \(f\) and \(g\) are not monic. Hint for (b): use @thm-coprime-divides-product .

title: Lemma 5.2.5 (Dividing Does Not Change the Ideal)
content: Let \(F\) be a field and \(f, g, q, r \in F[x]\) with \(f = qg + r\) . Then \(\langle f, g \rangle = \langle g, r \rangle\) . Consequently \(\gcd(f, g) = \gcd(g, r)\) .

title: Proposition 5.2.7 (Coprime Means 1 Is a Combination)
content: Let \(F\) be a field and \(f, g \in F[x]\) . Then \(f\) and \(g\) are coprime if and only if there exist \(a, b \in F[x]\) with \(af + bg = 1\) .

title: Proposition 5.2.9 (The gcd Is the Same Over a Larger Field)
content: Let \(K\) be a subfield of a field \(L\) , and let \(f, g \in K[x]\) . Then the greatest common divisor of \(f\) and \(g\) computed in \(K[x]\) equals the one computed in \(L[x]\) . In particular, \(f\) and \(g\) are coprime over \(K\) if and only if they are coprime over \(L\) .

title: Proposition 5.2.1 (The Ideal Generated by Finitely Many Polynomials)
content: Let \(F\) be a field and \(f_1, \dots, f_k \in F[x]\) , with \(k \ge 1\) . Then \(\langle f_1, \dots, f_k \rangle\) is an ideal of \(F[x]\) containing \(f_1, \dots, f_k\) . Moreover, every ideal \(J\) of \(F[x]\) with \(f_1, \dots, f_k \in J\) satisfies \(\langle f_1, \dots, f_k \rangle \subseteq J\) .

title: Theorem 5.2.8 (A Coprime Factor Can Be Canceled)
content: Let \(F\) be a field and \(p, q, r \in F[x]\) . If \(p \mid qr\) and \(\gcd(p, q) = 1\) , then \(p \mid r\) .

title: Theorem 5.2.6 (Euclidean Algorithm)
content:
Let \(F\) be a field and \(f, g \in F[x]\) with \(g 
eq 0\) . Put \(r_{-1} = f\) and \(r_0 = g\) . As long as \(r_k 
eq 0\) , divide \(r_{k-1}\) by \(r_k\) ( @thm-polynomial-division ): \[ r_{k-1} = q_{k+1} r_k + r_{k+1}, \qquad \deg r_{k+1} < \deg r_k . \] Then: the process stops: there is an index \(n\) with \(0 \le n \le \deg g\) such that \(r_n 
eq 0\) and \(r_{n+1} = 0\) ; if \(c\) is the leading coefficient of this last non-zero remainder \(r_n\) , then \(\gcd(f, g) = c^{-1} r_n\) .

title: Theorem 5.2.3 (Characterization of the gcd)
content: Let \(F\) be a field, \(f, g \in F[x]\) , and \(d = \gcd(f, g)\) . \(d \mid f\) and \(d \mid g\) . If \(h \in F[x]\) satisfies \(h \mid f\) and \(h \mid g\) , then \(h \mid d\) . If \(f, g\) are not both zero, then \(d\) is the only monic polynomial with properties (a) and (b).

title: Theorem 5.2.2 (Every Ideal of F\lbrack x\rbrack Is Principal)
content: Let \(F\) be a field and \(I\) an ideal of \(F[x]\) . If \(I \neq \{0\}\) , there is exactly one monic polynomial \(d\) with \(I = \langle d \rangle\) . Moreover, \(d\) is the unique monic polynomial of least degree in \(I\) .

title: Corollary 5.3.4 (Euclid’s Lemma for Several Factors)
content: Let \(F\) be a field and \(p \in F[x]\) irreducible over \(F\) . If \(q_1, \dots, q_k \in F[x]\) with \(k \ge 1\) and \(p \mid q_1 q_2 \cdots q_k\) , then \(p \mid q_i\) for some \(i\) . If \(q\) is irreducible over \(F\) , \(p \mid q\) , and \(p, q\) are both monic, then \(p = q\) .

title: Definition 5.3.1 (Irreducible Polynomial)
content: Let \(F\) be a field. A polynomial \(p \in F[x]\) is irreducible over \(F\) if \(p\) is non-constant , that is, \(\deg p \ge 1\) ; and whenever \(p = gh\) with \(g, h \in F[x]\) , one of \(g, h\) is a constant. A non-constant polynomial that is not irreducible is reducible over \(F\) .

title: Example (A Cubic That Is Irreducible Over \nQ)
content: Decide whether \(f = 2x^3 - 3x^2 + 4x - 1\) is irreducible over \(\nQ\) .

title: Example (Irreducible Polynomials of Every Degree Over \nQ)
content: Show that \(x^n - 2\) is irreducible over \(\nQ\) for every \(n \ge 1\) . (b) Show that \(x^4 + 10x + 5\) is irreducible over \(\nQ\) .

content: Let \(F\) be a field, \(p \in F[x]\) irreducible over \(F\) , and \(f \in F[x]\) . Then either \(p \mid f\) or \(\gcd(p, f) = 1\) .

mid a_0\) . Then \(f\) is irreducible over \(
Q\) .

title: Theorem 5.3.3 (Euclid’s Lemma for Polynomials)
content: Let \(F\) be a field and \(p \in F[x]\) irreducible over \(F\) . If \(q, r \in F[x]\) and \(p \mid qr\) , then \(p \mid q\) or \(p \mid r\) .

title: Theorem 5.3.1 (Irreducibility in Degree 2 and 3)
content: Let \(F\) be a field and \(p \in F[x]\) . \(p\) has a factor of degree \(1\) in \(F[x]\) if and only if \(p\) has a root in \(F\) . In particular, if \(\deg p \ge 2\) and \(p\) has a root in \(F\) , then \(p\) is reducible over \(F\) . If \(\deg p \in \{2, 3\}\) , then \(p\) is irreducible over \(F\) if and only if \(p\) has no root in \(F\) .

title: Theorem 5.3.6 (Rational Root Theorem)
content:
Let \(f = a_n x^n + a_{n-1} x^{n-1} + \dots + a_0 \in 
Z[x]\) with \(n \ge 1\) and \(a_n 
eq 0\) . If \(u/v \in 
Q\) is in lowest terms and \(f(u/v) = 0\) , then \(u \mid a_0\) and \(v \mid a_n\) .

title: Theorem 5.3.5 (Unique Factorization in F\lbrack x\rbrack)
content: Let \(F\) be a field and \(f \in F[x]\) non-constant. Existence. There are a non-zero constant \(c \in F\) , an integer \(k \ge 1\) , and monic polynomials \(p_1, \dots, p_k \in F[x]\) , each irreducible over \(F\) , with \[ f = c \, p_1 p_2 \cdots p_k . \] Uniqueness. If also \(f = c' \, q_1 q_2 \cdots q_l\) with \(c' \in F\) non-zero, \(l \ge 1\) , and \(q_1, \dots, q_l\) monic and irreducible over \(F\) , then \(c = c'\) , \(k = l\) , and after renumbering the \(q_j\) we have \(p_i = q_i\) for every \(i\) . In both factorizations, the constant is the leading coefficient of \(f\) .

title: Corollary 5.4.6 (Repeated Factors and \gcd(f, f'))
content: Let \(F\) be a field and \(f \in F[x]\) non-constant. ( Any field. ) If \(p \in F[x]\) is irreducible and \(p^2 \mid f\) , then \(p \mid \gcd(f, f')\) . Hence, if \(\gcd(f, f') = 1\) , then no irreducible polynomial divides \(f\) twice; in particular \(f\) has no multiple root in \(F\) . ( Characteristic \(0\) . ) If \(F\) has characteristic \(0\) and \(\gcd(f, f') \neq 1\) , then \(p^2 \mid f\) for some irreducible \(p \in F[x]\) .

title: Definition 5.4.3 (Formal Derivative)
content: Let \(F\) be a field and \(f = a_0 + a_1x + \dots + a_nx^n \in F[x]\) . The formal derivative of \(f\) is \[ f' = a_1 + 2a_2x + 3a_3x^2 + \dots + na_nx^{n-1} = \sum_{k=1}^{n} k a_k x^{k-1} , \] where \(ka_k\) is the integer multiple of \(a_k\) (the sum of \(k\) copies of \(a_k\) ). Higher derivatives are defined by \(f^{(0)} = f\) and \(f^{(k+1)} = (f^{(k)})'\) ; we also write \(f'' = f^{(2)}\) .

title: Definition 5.4.2 (Splitting into Linear Factors)
content: Let \(F\) be a field. A non-zero \(f \in F[x]\) of degree \(n\) splits over \(F\) if there are \(a \in F\) and \(a_1, \dots, a_n \in F\) , not necessarily distinct, with \[ f = a(x - a_1)(x - a_2) \cdots (x - a_n) . \]

title: Definition 5.4.1 (Multiplicity of a Root)
content: Let \(F\) be a field, \(f \in F[x]\) non-zero and \(c \in F\) . The multiplicity of \(c\) as a root of \(f\) , written \(\operatorname{mult}_c(f)\) , is the largest \(m \in \nN\) such that \((x - c)^m \mid f\) . The root \(c\) is simple if \(\operatorname{mult}_c(f) = 1\) , and multiple (or repeated ) if \(\operatorname{mult}_c(f) \ge 2\) .

title: Example (Detecting a Repeated Root with a gcd)
content: Decide whether \(f = x^4 - 2x^3 + 2x - 1 \in \nQ[x]\) has a repeated irreducible factor, using only \(\gcd(f, f')\) . Does \(f\) have a multiple root in \(\nC\) ?

title: Example (Finding a Multiplicity by Repeated Division)
content: Let \(f = x^4 - 2x^3 + 2x - 1 \in \nQ[x]\) . Find the multiplicity of \(1\) and of \(-1\) as roots of \(f\) .

title: Example (Re-centering a Cubic)
content: Expand \(f = x^3 - 2x + 5 \in \nQ[x]\) in powers of \(x - 1\) .

content:
Let \(f = x^5 - 3x^4 + 4x^3 - 4x^2 + 3x - 1\) . Find \(\operatorname{mult}_1(f)\) in \(

title: Exercise (B3: The multiplicity of 1)
content: Let \(n \ge 2\) and \(f = x^n - nx + n - 1 \in \nQ[x]\) . Prove that \(1\) is a root of \(f\) of multiplicity exactly \(2\) .

title: Exercise (C1: Real roots of the derivative)
content:
Let \(f \in 
R[x]\) have degree \(n \ge 2\) and split over \(

title: Exercise (C2: x^p - x over \nF_p)
content:
Let \(p\) be a prime and \(f = x^p - x \in 
F_p[x]\) . Compute \(f'\) and deduce that \(f\) has no repeated irreducible factor. Using @exr-polynomials-c2 , deduce that \(x^p - x = \prod_{a \in 
F_p} (x - a)\) . Explain why the argument of (a) gives nothing for \(g = x^p - 1\) . Then prove that \(g = (x - 1)^p\) in \(
F_p[x]\) . Hint for (c): for \(0 < k < p\) , use the integer identity \(k inom{p}{k} = p inom{p-1}{k-1}\) .

title: Exercise (C3: Removing repeated factors)
content: Let \(F\) be a field and \(f = a\,p_1^{e_1} \cdots p_r^{e_r} \in F[x]\) , where \(a \in F \setminus \{0\}\) , the \(p_i\) are distinct monic irreducible polynomials and \(e_i \ge 1\) . Suppose \(F\) has characteristic \(0\) . Prove that \(\gcd(f, f') = p_1^{e_1 - 1} \cdots p_r^{e_r - 1}\) , and deduce that \(f / \gcd(f, f') = a\,p_1 \cdots p_r\) . Over \(\nF_2\) , let \(f = x^2(x + 1)\) . Compute \(f / \gcd(f, f')\) and show that the conclusion of (a) fails. Hint for (a): write \(D = p_1^{e_1-1}\cdots p_r^{e_r-1}\) . Show \(D \mid \gcd(f, f')\) ; for the reverse, show \(p_i^{e_i} \nmid f'\) using Euclid’s lemma.

title: Lemma 5.4.1 (Multiplicity via the Cofactor)
content: Let \(f \in F[x]\) be non-zero, \(c \in F\) and \(m \in \nN\) . Then \(\operatorname{mult}_c(f) = m\) if and only if \[ f = (x - c)^m g \quad \text{for some } g \in F[x] \text{ with } g(c) \neq 0 . \]

title: Theorem 5.4.4 (Rules for the Formal Derivative)
content: Let \(F\) be a field, \(f, g \in F[x]\) , \(a, b, c \in F\) and \(m \ge 1\) an integer. Then: \((af + bg)' = af' + bg'\) , and \(a' = 0\) for the constant polynomial \(a\) ; \((fg)' = f'g + fg'\) (product rule); \((g^m)' = m\,g^{m-1}g'\) ; in particular \(\bigl((x - c)^m\bigr)' = m(x - c)^{m-1}\) .

title: Theorem 5.4.2 (Multiplicity of a Product)
content: Let \(f, g \in F[x]\) be non-zero and \(c \in F\) . Then \(\operatorname{mult}_c(fg) = \operatorname{mult}_c(f) + \operatorname{mult}_c(g)\) .

title: Theorem 5.4.7 (Taylor Expansion of a Polynomial)
content: Let \(F\) be a field, \(n \in \nN\) and \(c \in F\) . The list \(\sB_c = \bigl(1, x - c, (x - c)^2, \dots, (x - c)^n\bigr)\) is a basis of \(F[x]_{\le n}\) . Suppose \(F\) has characteristic \(0\) , or characteristic \(p > n\) . For \(k = 0, \dots, n\) define \(\varphi_k \colon F[x]_{\le n} \to F\) by \(\varphi_k(f) = \dfrac{f^{(k)}(c)}{k!}\) . Then \((\varphi_0, \dots, \varphi_n)\) is the dual basis of \(\sB_c\) , and every \(f \in F[x]_{\le n}\) satisfies \[ f = \sum_{k=0}^{n} \frac{f^{(k)}(c)}{k!}\,(x - c)^k . \]

title: Theorem 5.4.5 (Repeated Root Test)
content: Let \(F\) be a field, \(f \in F[x]\) non-zero and \(c \in F\) . \(c\) is a multiple root of \(f\) if and only if \(f(c) = 0\) and \(f'(c) = 0\) . Suppose \(\operatorname{mult}_c(f) = m \ge 1\) and \(m \cdot 1 \neq 0\) in \(F\) (this holds automatically if \(F\) has characteristic \(0\) ). Then \(f' \neq 0\) and \(\operatorname{mult}_c(f') = m - 1\) .

title: Theorem 5.4.3 (Roots Counted with Multiplicity)
content: Let \(F\) be a field and \(f \in F[x]\) non-zero. Let \(c_1, \dots, c_k\) be the distinct roots of \(f\) in \(F\) , with multiplicities \(m_1, \dots, m_k\) . Then \[ f = (x - c_1)^{m_1} \cdots (x - c_k)^{m_k}\, g \] for some \(g \in F[x]\) with no root in \(F\) . Consequently \[ m_1 + \dots + m_k \le \deg f , \] with equality if and only if \(f\) splits over \(F\) .

title: Corollary 5.5.5 (Complex Polynomials Split)
content:
Every non-zero \(p \in 
C[x]\) splits over \(
C\) : if \(\deg p = n\) and \(p\) has leading coefficient \(a\) , then \(p = a(x - z_1)(x - z_2)\cdots(x - z_n)\) for some \(z_1, \dots, z_n \in 
C\) . In particular the multiplicities of the roots of \(p\) add up to \(n\) . The irreducible polynomials in \(
C[x]\) are exactly the polynomials of degree \(1\) .

title: Corollary 5.5.9 (Odd Degree Forces a Real Root)
content: Every \(f \in \nR[x]\) of odd degree has a root in \(\nR\) .

title: Corollary 5.5.8 (Factorization over \nR)
content:
Every non-constant \(f \in 
R[x]\) can be written as \[ f = a\,(x - c_1)\cdots(x - c_r)\;q_1\cdots q_s , \] where \(a \in 
R\) is the leading coefficient of \(f\) , \(c_1, \dots, c_r \in 
R\) (not necessarily distinct), and \(q_1, \dots, q_s \in 
R[x]\) are monic quadratics with no real root. Then \(r + 2s = \deg f\) , and \(r\) is the sum of the multiplicities of the real roots of \(f\) . The factorization is unique up to the order of the factors.

title: Corollary 5.5.7 (Irreducible Real Polynomials)
content: The irreducible polynomials in \(\nR[x]\) are exactly the polynomials of degree \(1\) , and the polynomials of degree \(2\) with no real root. In particular, every irreducible polynomial in \(\nR[x]\) has degree \(1\) or \(2\) .

title: Example (One Step Downhill)
content: Let \(p = x^3 + x^2 + 1 \in \nC[x]\) and \(z_0 = 0\) . Follow the proof of @lem-dalembert to find \(z\) with \(\lvert p(z) \rvert < \lvert p(0) \rvert\) .

title: Example (Factoring x^4 + 1 over \nC and over \nR)
content: Factor \(f = x^4 + 1\) into irreducible polynomials in \(\nC[x]\) and in \(\nR[x]\) .

Follow the proof of @lem-dalembert at \(z_0 = 0\) : find \(k\) , \(B\) , \(u\) and \(t\) , and verify that \(\lvert p(tu) \rvert < \lvert p(0) \rvert\) . Compute \(p(i/2)\) , and explain why the direction \(i\) does not work here, although it did in @exm-dalembert-step .

content:

content:

content:
Let \(p \in 
C[x]\) be non-constant, and let \(z_0 \in 
C\) with \(p(z_0) 
eq 0\) . Then there is \(z \in 
C\) with \(\lvert p(z) vert < \lvert p(z_0) vert\) .

content:
Let \(p \in 
C[x]\) . Then there is \(z_0 \in 
C\) with \(\lvert p(z_0) vert \le \lvert p(z) vert\) for every \(z \in
